opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: New Projects and Commissions max £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections max £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications max £5,000; Long-Term Research max £20,000; Research and Travel max £2,500

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating non-profit for at least 12 months) for most categories; individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators for the Research and Travel category. Not open to individuals independently developing their own artistic practice.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and research expanding the appreciation of sculpture. Categories: New Projects and Commissions (exhibitions, catalogues, commissions); Acquisitions and Collections; Conferences, Lectures and Publications; Long-Term Research; and Research and Travel grants for individuals. Applications considered four times per year; the Autumn round is currently open.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation for travel and subsistence: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000; plus accommodation in Leeds or Hertfordshire

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics, curators, artists and researchers working on historic and contemporary sculpture. Research Fellowships at the Institute for academics/curators; Artist Research Fellowships for artists; Senior Fellowships for established scholars. Fellowships at Studios & Gardens only for projects related to Henry Moore.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships enabling researchers to spend a month using the Henry Moore Institute's facilities in Leeds or Henry Moore Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence. Applications for 2026/27 are closed; the next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: BA dissertation £250 cash prize; MA dissertation £250 cash prize; plus Henry Moore Institute publications to the value of £50, copies added to the Research Library, and publication of abstracts

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines whose dissertation was submitted within the past academic year at a UK university. Dissertations must relate directly to sculpture and not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Two annual prizes for outstanding extended writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture, open to BA and MA students. The 2025 prize deadline has passed; submissions for the next prize open in autumn.
